title: s[TOR-Y]telling Demo is available!
author: No-Grass-2256
selftext:
**s\[TOR-Y\]telling** is a sandbox + visual novel (Ren'Py) where a Llama-based LLM generates the characters' dialogue and branches the story around your choices — running **100% locally/offline**: privacy-first, no API costs, works with no internet.

It ships with 50 hand-authored scenarios plus an AI-assisted custom-story mode, so it's a blend of generative open-endedness and authored narrative.

Free demo + wishlist: store.steampowered.com/app/4295120 · linktr.ee/curious\_biped

Glad to get into the detail on local inference, character/prompt design, or the sandbox↔VN loop.

replies.author: No-Grass-2256
replies.body: The idea behind the project is to show that local AI is fun. One thing that I may say is that s\[TOR-Y\]telling has a unique gameplay loop. It has a generative sandbox, which is AI-driven indeed, but your actions on the sandbox connect with classic Visual Novel storytelling. In which other game could you try to avoid torture from a Yakuza thug by claiming to be Santa Claus? Or could you argue with your cat about it typing bad names to your boss yesterday? There is an entire branch of the game that has no script and that is fresh. Try the demo, it could surprise you.

comments.author: AssistBorn4589
comments.body:
> 1. Local Operation: s[TOR-Y]telling is a local, single-player sandbox tool. The Developer does not monitor, collect, or host the stories or images created or imported by the User.

> 3. PROHIBITED CONTENT & CONDUCT:

> 4. AI Safety: This software includes a "Strict Policy" filter to prevent the generation of illegal or harmful content. Attempting to bypass these filters is a violation of this License.

Maybe take your choice and stand with it? Either it is local tool where user is responsible _or_ you have content policy that can result in loss of access.

Plus, sorry, but I'm not paying for "I have to stop you here" generator.

replies.author: No-Grass-2256
replies.body: Since s\[TOR-Y\]telling is a product on a platform it has to comply with some rules. One of my personal goals with the project was to achieve a good compromise between Steam required safety and freedom. The alternatives are applications that you must have the headache of setting everything to make the process just work (model, parameters, and prompts). Setting SillyTavern is difficult, for example. It has more freedom indeed, but s\[TOR-Y\]telling is a closed product that you may just run without worrying about how to make it work. Thank for your honest feedback on the premise. If you would like to play the demo and provide additional feedback, I would be glad to iterate over it on next updates.
